headline: High: shared-file prompt injection and data leakage are plausible because pdf.js reads PDFs while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads via broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and runs in browser-based tests, so malicious PDF content could be rendered as attacker-controlled text. social-auto-upload processes media/account workflows and could consume exported PDF-derived content if the operator bridges outputs manually. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the operator copies pdf.js-rendered text into social-auto-upload inputs, injection becomes reachable.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace, attacker-controlled PDF content can propagate.
mitigations: Render PDFs in a quarantined viewer before passing text onward.
Disable any copy-paste bridge between the two agents during review.
Use separate workspaces for PDF intake and upload preparation.
Add a manual approval step before social-auto-upload consumes extracted text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents, while social-auto-upload touches account data and has broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or the PDF contains sensitive material, content can flow from local document processing into an external upload path. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so uncertainty is escalated to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF PDF documents contain sensitive personal or business data and are fed into the upload workflow, leakage is possible.
IF the operator stores both agents' inputs in one directory, cross-exposure becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep PDF inputs and upload assets in separate directories.
Strip sensitive pages before any upload workflow.
Review outbound destinations for social-auto-upload before use.
Use test accounts and dummy documents for dry runs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests, while social-auto-upload also supports multiple instances but cannot write files or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource conflict is limited. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable directory not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable directory, contention becomes possible.
IF the operator adds shared OAuth or git state outside the profiles, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Avoid shared git repositories for the pair.
Serialize any handoff through a single operator step.
Document ownership of each file path before running both agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted or rendered document content, and social-auto-upload can act on media/account workflows with broad network egress. If the operator treats pdf.js output as authoritative and feeds it into upload actions without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect public posts or account-side actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is used as the source of truth for upload metadata, cascading errors are reachable.
IF social-auto-upload auto-publishes without a human review step, bad upstream content can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text before upload.
Compare pdf.js output against the original PDF for critical fields.
Use a staging account for first-pass uploads.
Add a checklist for title, caption, and attachment verification.

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF documents locally and social-auto-upload handles account data plus media uploads. The profiles do not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII, nor a residency mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible. Because social-auto-upload has broad egress and account-data handling, the operator should still verify retention and platform policy alignment.
conditions: IF the PDFs contain regulated personal data and are uploaded through social-auto-upload, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the operator retains uploaded media or account data beyond policy limits, a retention mismatch exists.
mitigations: Classify the PDFs before any upload.
Avoid uploading regulated data through the pair.
Check retention settings for the upload platform.
Use a deletion/export procedure for test accounts.
